main_text.p: mari dicuntur? Cassander ille (qui Coloniae resipuit ante obitum, & indicta sua cupiens, professioni fidei Pii IV. pag.218. subscripsit) saltem occasionem dat explicandi negotium; si tamen id meretur peculiarem operam, inspicerem observationes Sacras Josephi Vicecomitis: verum mon reperiuntur in hisce regionibus: porro unum necessarium est. Magne vir, Deus te conservet Ecclesiæ suæ bono, seu splendori potius, ut conservavit hactenus.

Est hic locorum vir aliqvis excellens, tui æstimantissimus, qui vocatur Leonardus Marius, is te cupit salvere plurimum, ut ego, si occasio tulerit, Veronium etiam ac Rigaltium; qui nec abjuravi scribere: deinceps quoque, nihil dissimulo, quia gaudio plenus, è literis tuis, Patrone exoptatissime, penitusque optime.
main_text.head: EPIST. LXVII. Abraham Ecchellensis Johanni Morino mittit capita Epitomes constitutio-num

page.notes: The word "Cassander" begins with a superscript "a" printed above the C, shown here as plain "Ca" in the original. The word "mon" in "verum mon reperiuntur" is printed in bold type, which is a printing irregularity and is kept as printed. The date "cIↄ IↄCXLIX." is an old Roman numeral form for MDCXLIX. The reference "pag.218." is in italic type. The letter-title line ends with the hyphenated word "constitutio-" continued as "num". No catchword, signature or marginal notes appear on this page.
